name: OK-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Josh Brecheen running for reelection
Democratic challenger raised only ~$4,300 with $86 on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~2%
model.rationale: This southeastern Oklahoma seat is deeply Republican, Brecheen is an incumbent with a large financial edge, and Brandon Wade's fundraising is negligible. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Republican hold.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or major outside spending against Brecheen is essentially the only path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oklahoma's 2nd District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and first-term incumbent Josh Brecheen is running for reelection with the advantages that come with incumbency in a safe seat. He has out-raised his Democratic challenger, Brandon Wade, by roughly fifty to one, and Wade's $86 in cash on hand leaves no realistic capacity to compete on the airwaves or in the field.

No public polls or expert ratings track this race, which itself signals how little competitive attention it draws. Prediction markets give Wade only about a 2% chance, consistent with the district's R+28 lean. A minor independent is also on the ballot but lacks visible resources. The forecast is a comfortable Republican win, with uncertainty driven mainly by turnout variation rather than genuine competition.
